title: Integral reduced algebras of finite generic dimension over a finite-type domain are finite
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $R$ be a commutative integral domain of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] (generated as a $k$-algebra by finitely many elements). Put $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. Let $S$ be a commutative reduced $R$-algebra (its only nilpotent element is zero). Assume that $S$ is torsion-free as an $R$-module, that every $s\in S$ satisfies a monic polynomial in $R[Z]$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and that the localization $S_Q=(R\setminus\{0\})^{-1}S=S\otimes_R Q$ is a finite-dimensional $Q$-vector space. Then $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. No finite-type hypothesis on $S$ is assumed; the zero algebra is allowed, and no separability hypothesis is imposed on the field factors of $S_Q$.

source.place: Agent assembly of Tags 00J6 and 00JB (finite-dimensional reduced generic fibre is a finite product of fields), Tag 0335 (finite normalization of a finite-type domain over a field in finite field extensions), and Tag 00IK (Noetherian submodules of finite modules). proof.text:
Put $T=S_Q$. The localization map $j:S	o T$ is injective: if $j(s)=0$, the fraction equality criterion gives $as=0$ for some $0
e a\in R$, so torsion-freeness gives $s=0$. Moreover $T$ is reduced. Indeed, if $(s/a)^n=0$ with $n\ge1$, then $bs^n=0$ for some $0
e b\in R$; torsion-freeness gives $s^n=0$ and reducedness gives $s=0$. These are direct fraction calculations. If $T=0$, injectivity gives $S=0$, generated by the empty family, and the conclusion holds. Henceforth assume $T
e0$.

source.place: Elementary localization calculation from the definitions of fractions, torsion-free module and reduced ring; agent assembly preceding Tag 00J6.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian], the finite-dimensional commutative $Q$-algebra $T$ is Artinian. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product] to this reduced Artinian ring: its maximal ideals form a finite set $I$, and the quotient maps give $T\simeq\prod_{i\in I}L_i$, where $L_i=T/\mathfrak m_i$ is a field. Give each $L_i$ its induced $Q$-algebra structure. The map $Q\to L_i$ is injective since it is unital between fields. Images in $L_i$ of a finite $Q$-basis of $T$ span $L_i$, so each $L_i/Q$ is a finite field extension. All structural maps are compatible with $R\to Q$.

For every $i\in I$ let $C_i$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $L_i$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] it is an $R$-subalgebra of $L_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-field-integral-closure-finite] with $k$, $A=R$, $K=Q$ and $L=L_i$. Its hypotheses hold: $R$ is a finite-type domain over $k$, $Q$ is its fraction field, and step 2 gives a finite field extension with the compatible algebra structures. Thus every $C_i$ is a finitely generated $R$-module. This theorem requires neither normality of $R$ nor separability of $L_i/Q$.

source.place: Tag 0335 (proposition-ubiquity-nagata), parts (1),(5), and N-2: normalization in arbitrary finite field extensions.

proof.text: The composite $S\xrightarrow{j}T\simeq\prod_iL_i$ takes values in $C=\prod_iC_i$: for $s\in S$, apply each component ring homomorphism to its given monic equation over $R$; the same monic equation annihilates its image in $L_i$. Thus it lies in $C_i$ by the definition used in step 3. This gives an injective $R$-linear map $f:S\to C$. The module $C$ is finite: choose finite generators for each $C_i$ and insert each generator into its coordinate, with zeros in the other coordinates. The resulting finite family spans $C$ by adding the coordinate expressions. The image $N=f(S)$ is an $R$-submodule of $C$, since $f(s)+f(t)=f(s+t)$ and $rf(s)=f(rs)$.

source.place: Elementary assembly from step 3: applying homomorphisms to monic equations and coordinatewise generation of finite products.

proof.text: By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], applied to the finite-type $k$-algebra $R$, the ring $R$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], its submodule $N\subseteq C$ is finitely generated. Choose generators $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ of $N$ and preimages $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in S$. For $s\in S$, write $f(s)=\sum_j a_jn_j$; linearity and injectivity give $s=\sum_j a_js_j$. Hence $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-module.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q29-1b96406f4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. It has no new nodes, the statement is unchanged, and there is no repair note, so this is an ordinary split. The statement is true: S embeds in the integral closure of R in the product of fields S_Q, and that closure is finite because R is Japanese (Stacks 0335 (1),(5)). I tested S=0, R=k, a cusp ring with its normalization k[t], and a purely inseparable extension in characteristic p. Step 1 is elementary and correct: S injects into S_Q by torsion-freeness, and S_Q is reduced. Step 2 cites finite-dim-algebra-artinian (applied with k=Q) and reduced-artinian-residue-product (reducedness comes from step 1), and the finite field factors L_i over Q follow correctly. Step 3 cites lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-field-integral-closure-finite with A=R, K=Q, L=L_i; the scalar tower is compatible, and there is no separability or normality hypothesis in either the node or its Lean signature. Step 4 is elementary: monic equations push forward into each L_i, the map into the product of the C_i is injective, and the product is finite. Step 5 uses the Noetherian clause of lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components and the submodule-finite lemma, then lifts generators through the injective map. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. The Stacks tag-to-label pairs (00FN, 00IK, 00J6, 00J7, 00JB, 0335) check out in tags/tags. A DAG search turned up no duplicate. The only citer, finite-affinoid-canonical-reduction, supplies every hypothesis. I accept the declared tool_use of lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-field-integral-closure-finite: it is generic normalization finiteness, and unit sk-i-curve-zero has nothing to replace it. No SGA is used and no fixes were needed.
